tagline: a harness for vision-language models (VLMs) that read and edit networks
eyebrow: PAVE · a harness for VLMs that read and edit networks
lead: A vision-language model reads imagery of the real road and writes into a GMNS network. The harness around it renders what the model sees, ties every answer to network IDs and image coordinates, checks each answer and returns failures with the reason, and records every step so a run can be replayed. The model makes the judgements; the harness measures, checks and edits.

stages.name: Perceive
stages.text: Satellite crops with rulers, street views tied to the network by camera pose, ID-marked drawings of the network. The model can ask for closer views.

stages.name: Anchor
stages.text: Every answer points at something that can be checked: a stop bar, a lane boundary in crop pixels, a link or node ID.

stages.name: Verify
stages.text: A real road gives no reward. Geometry checks, street-view lane counts, proposal gates and network and design checks stand in.

stages.name: Edit
stages.text: Lanes, lane use and movements written to GMNS, or a new design built from templates and exported as GMNS tables and a project card.

loop_back: a failed check goes back to the model with the reason

edit.title: SR 347 / I-10 interchange, Arizona
edit.context: The model names the existing links that make up the interchange. A template builds each alternative from them, and checks verify the result before it is written back as GMNS.
edit.text: The existing diamond is rebuilt as a diverging diamond, a single point urban interchange or roundabout ramp terminals. The model names the links involved, templates build each design, and checks verify it.
facts: proposal gates passed by the first answer

principles: The model reads rendered imagery, not a text dump of the network. Every source image is kept and can be looked at again.
The harness measures, the model judges
Code computes positions, widths, headings and projections; open questions go to the model as choices among candidates.
Stop-bar positions, boundary coordinates, link and node IDs, each with the image region it relies on.
Geometry, cross-view and network checks decide whether an answer stands; a failure returns with the reason for another try.
Prompts, images and raw answers are kept, so a run can be repeated or extended without new model calls.
The same interface has run with different vision-language models; the model is a parameter, not part of the design.
